definitionEn: to gradually move into a bad state, such as chaos or violence
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — спускаться (по лестнице, с горы). Здесь — descend into: скатиться в хаос, перерасти в ссору.
situation: A meeting, event or country gradually becomes chaotic, violent or unpleasant and gets out of control.

examples.text: The budget meeting quickly [[descended]] into a shouting match.
Within hours, the peaceful protest had [[descended]] into violence.
Every family dinner seems to [[descend]] into an argument about politics.

texts: The group chat [[descended]] into insults after the vote.
By midnight the party had [[descended]] into chaos.
The debate soon [[descended]] into personal attacks.

badCollocation.noteRu: В этом значении descend требует into: descend into chaos. «In» или «to» здесь — ошибка.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Descend into chaos — скатиться в хаос. Lower — опускать что-то, drop — падать или ронять, reduce — сокращать; с into chaos они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The friendly match [[descended]] into an ugly row between the two teams.
nuance.explanationRu: Descend into — перерасти во что-то плохое: хаос, драку, ссору. Decline — постепенно снижаться (о числах, здоровье, качестве), в конкретное событие не «перерастает».

reverse.explanationRu: Продажи, цены и показатели снижаются — decline. Descend в переносном смысле — это descend into chaos или violence.

fixIt.text: The small disagreement quickly [[outgrew]] into a full-scale row.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Перерасти в ссору» — descend into a row (или turn into). Outgrow — «вырасти из» (одежды, увлечения), с into не употребляется.

wordFormation.text: The film follows one family's slow [[descent]] into poverty.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was the neighbours' barbecue last night?"
options: Honestly, it descended into a really lovely, relaxed evening.
Fun at first, but it descended into a row about parking by nine.
The gathering regrettably descended into disorder, as I had formally predicted.
reply.explanationRu: Descend into — скатиться во что-то плохое, как вечеринка в ссору. «Descended into a lovely evening» — противоречие, а третий ответ звучит как протокол, а не рассказ другу.

definitionEn: a person's family origins, especially their nationality or ethnic background
senseNote: Также descent — спуск (самолёта, по склону); здесь — происхождение: of Italian descent.
situation: You say which country or ethnic group someone's parents, grandparents or ancestors came from.

examples.text: She was born in Toronto but is of Portuguese [[descent]].
Many people in the region can trace their [[descent]] back to Viking settlers.
The chef, who is of mixed Korean and Mexican [[descent]], combines both cuisines on her menu.

texts: Around a third of the town's residents are of Polish [[descent]].
His surname hints at his French [[descent]].
Citizenship can sometimes be claimed through [[descent]] from a grandparent.

badCollocation.noteRu: Потомок — descendant: a descendant of a famous poet. Descent — происхождение, а не человек.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Of Nigerian descent — нигерийского происхождения. Roots используют иначе (she has Nigerian roots), а of Nigerian family и generation так не говорят.

nuance.text: He claims direct [[descent]] from a medieval king.
nuance.explanationRu: Descent — родство по линии предков: direct descent from a king. Origin — происхождение вообще, в том числе слов и вещей; «origin from a king» не говорят.

reverse.text: Nobody knows the [[origin]] of this strange tradition.
reverse.explanationRu: Происхождение слова, обычая или вещи — origin. Descent — только о семье и предках человека.

fixIt.text: My grandmother was of Greek [[descendant]], though she never learned the language.
fixIt.explanationRu: Of Greek descent — греческого происхождения. Descendant — «потомок», то есть человек, а не происхождение.

wordFormation.text: He is a direct [[descendant]] of the town's founder.

rewrite.original: Her parents and grandparents all came from Japan.

definitionEn: to officially choose something or someone for a particular purpose or status
senseNote: Реже — «обозначать» (на карте, в документе); здесь — официально объявлять или назначать.
situation: An authority officially decides that a place, building or person will have a particular role or status.

examples.text: The forest was [[designated]] a national park in 1998.
Each team should [[designate]] one person to handle customer complaints.
This land has been [[designated]] for affordable housing, not offices.

texts: Smoking is only allowed in [[designated]] areas.
She was [[designated]] as the manager's successor last year.
The city has [[designated]] three streets as car-free zones.

collocations: [[designate]] an area as a national park

badCollocation.noteRu: «Назначить встречу» — arrange или set up a meeting. Designate — официально определить статус или роль места или человека.

collocationTask.prompt: The area has been ___ a nature reserve.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Статус заповедника территории присваивают: be designated a nature reserve. Appoint, nominate и elect — про людей и должности.

nuance.text: The building has been [[designated]] a historic monument, so it cannot be demolished.
nuance.explanationRu: Designate — официально присвоить месту статус. Assign — поручить или выделить что-то кому-то: assign a task, assign a room to a guest.

reverse.text: Each new employee is [[assigned]] a mentor for the first month.
reverse.explanationRu: Выделить человеку наставника, задание или комнату — assign. «Is designated a mentor» означало бы, что сотрудника самого назначили наставником.

fixIt.text: In 2015 the old port was [[appointed]] a protected historic site.
fixIt.explanationRu: Appoint — назначить человека на должность. Статус месту присваивают глаголом designate: was designated a historic site.

wordFormation.text: The [[designation]] of the bay as a marine reserve has helped fish stocks recover.

rewrite.original: The council officially declared the old market a historic site.
rewrite.frame: The old market ____ a historic site by the council.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: something was designated a historic site.

definitionEn: preferred or advisable, though not absolutely necessary
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — привлекательный, желанный (a desirable area). Здесь — «желательный, но не обязательный», как в вакансиях и правилах.
situation: A job advert or a set of rules mentions something that would be good to have but is not required.

examples.text: A driving licence is [[desirable]] but not essential for this role.
It is [[desirable]] that all visitors wash their hands before entering the ward.
Some knowledge of statistics is [[desirable]] before you start the course.

texts: Fluent Spanish is [[desirable]] for this position.
A quick decision would be [[desirable]], but it is not urgent.
Is a university degree essential or merely [[desirable]]?

badCollocation.noteRu: Эффект, которого добивались, — the desired effect. Desirable — «желательный», а не «желаемый, запланированный».

collocationTask.explanationRu: В вакансиях: desirable but not essential — «желательно, но не обязательно». Hopeful — полный надежды, longing — тоскующий, а wanting — «недостаточный».

nuance.text: Good presentation skills are [[desirable]] for this role.
nuance.explanationRu: Desirable — желательный (о навыках, условиях). Wishful — «принимающий желаемое за действительное»: wishful thinking.

reverse.text: Expecting the train to be on time is just [[wishful]] thinking.
reverse.explanationRu: Несбыточная надежда — wishful thinking, устойчивое выражение. Desirable thinking так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Knowledge of German is [[preferential]] but not essential for this post.
fixIt.explanationRu: Preferential — «льготный» (preferential treatment). «Желательно, но не обязательно» — desirable but not essential.

wordFormation.text: For people with high blood pressure, a low-salt diet is highly [[desirable]].

reply.context: A friend applying for a job says: "The advert says 'Spanish desirable'. Should I still apply? I don't speak it."
options: No, desirable means they'll only hire native Spanish speakers.
Your application is desirable and shall be duly considered by the panel.
Definitely apply. Desirable just means it's a bonus, not a must.
reply.explanationRu: Desirable в вакансии — «желательно, но не обязательно», так что подавать стоит. Первый ответ искажает смысл, а второй звучит как письмо отдела кадров, а не совет другу.

definitionEn: the main screen of a computer, where icons, files and open windows appear
senseNote: Здесь — рабочий стол на экране. Desktop также значит «настольный компьютер» (в отличие от ноутбука).
situation: You talk about the main computer screen where you keep shortcuts, folders and files you use often.

examples.text: Save the file to your [[desktop]] so you can find it quickly.
My [[desktop]] is covered in old screenshots that I never delete.
The IT team put a shortcut to the new booking system on everyone's [[desktop]].

texts: Drag the folder onto the [[desktop]] and rename it.
A cluttered [[desktop]] makes it harder to find anything.
She changed her [[desktop]] background to a photo of her dog.

badCollocation.noteRu: Главный экран телефона — home screen. Desktop — рабочий стол компьютера.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Фон рабочего стола — desktop background (или wallpaper). Table и worktable — столы как мебель, office — офис.

nuance.text: Drag the icon off the [[desktop]] and into the folder.
nuance.explanationRu: Desktop — вся область экрана с иконками и окнами. Wallpaper — только фоновая картинка на нём.

reverse.text: I set a photo of the mountains as my [[wallpaper]].
reverse.explanationRu: Картинку на фоне называют wallpaper (или desktop background). Desktop — сам рабочий стол, а не картинка.

fixIt.text: I've saved the presentation on the [[work table]] of your laptop.
fixIt.explanationRu: Рабочий стол компьютера — desktop. Work table — стол как мебель, например в мастерской.

reply.context: An IT technician on the phone asks: "Can you see a folder called 'Invoices' anywhere?"
options: Yes, it's right there on my desktop, next to the recycle bin.
Yes, it's under my desktop, next to my shoes and bag.
Affirmative; the aforementioned folder is visible upon my desktop.
reply.explanationRu: On my desktop — на рабочем столе компьютера. «Под рабочим столом рядом с туфлями» — это уже desk, мебель, а третий ответ звучит неестественно официально.

definitionEn: causing serious harm to people's feelings, relationships or well-being
senseNote: Базовое значение (B1) — разрушительный (об урагане, войне). Здесь — вредный для людей и отношений: destructive criticism, a destructive relationship.
situation: Behaviour, habits or criticism slowly damage a person's confidence, health or relationships.

examples.text: It took her years to leave a [[destructive]] relationship that had cut her off from her friends.
Constant [[destructive]] criticism from her manager made her doubt every decision.
Gambling can become a [[destructive]] habit that ruins whole families.

texts: Jealousy is one of the most [[destructive]] emotions.
Her perfectionism had become quietly [[destructive]].
Drinking to cope with stress is a [[destructive]] pattern.

badCollocation.noteRu: Разрушенное здание — a destroyed или ruined building. Destructive — тот, кто разрушает, а не тот, кто пострадал.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Критика, которая только ранит, — destructive criticism (противоположность constructive). Destroying и damaged так не говорят, а ruinous — «разорительный».

nuance.text: His [[destructive]] comments about her weight slowly ruined her confidence.
nuance.explanationRu: Destructive — причиняющий вред (самооценке, отношениям). Disruptive — мешающий, нарушающий порядок: disruptive pupils, disruptive noise.

reverse.text: Roadworks outside the office have been very [[disruptive]] this week.
reverse.explanationRu: Ремонт дороги мешает работать — это disruptive. Destructive означало бы, что он что-то разрушает.

fixIt.text: His [[destroying]] behaviour eventually pushed all his friends away.
fixIt.explanationRu: Прилагательное «разрушительный» — destructive. Destroying — форма глагола destroy, перед существительным в этом смысле не используется.

wordFormation.text: Years of heavy drinking had a [[destructive]] effect on his marriage.

reply.context: A friend says: "My boss tore my report apart in front of everyone, but didn't say how to improve it."
options: That isn't feedback, that's just destructive criticism. You deserve better.
Well, at least it was destructive, so now you know exactly what to fix.
Such destructive commentary is, regrettably, most unbecoming of management.
reply.explanationRu: Destructive criticism — критика, которая ранит, но не помогает. Во втором ответе слово понято как «полезный», а третий звучит слишком книжно для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: to officially hold someone and not allow them to leave
situation: Police, border officials or security staff hold a person and do not allow them to go.

examples.text: Police [[detained]] three men after the fight outside the stadium.
She was [[detained]] at the airport for six hours because of a problem with her visa.
Under the new law, suspects can be [[detained]] for up to fourteen days without charge.

texts: Two journalists were [[detained]] while covering the protests.
He was [[detained]] at the border and later released.
The suspect will be [[detained]] in a police cell overnight.

badCollocation.noteRu: Задержанный рейс — a delayed flight. Detain — задерживать людей (полиция, охрана), а не транспорт.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Detained without charge — задержан без предъявления обвинения. Официальное обвинение — charge; accusation — упрёк, blame — вина, guilt — чувство вины.

nuance.text: Police [[detained]] two teenagers for questioning after the burglary.
nuance.explanationRu: Detain — официально задержать человека (полиция, пограничники). Delay — задержать в смысле «заставить опоздать»: рейс, поезд, проект.

reverse.text: Our train was [[delayed]] by almost two hours.
reverse.explanationRu: Поезд, рейс или посылка задерживаются — delayed. Detain — только о людях, которых удерживают власти.

fixIt.text: Two protesters were [[retained]] by police for several hours before being released.
fixIt.explanationRu: Retain — сохранять, удерживать у себя (retain staff, retain heat). Людей под стражей держат: detain.

wordFormation.text: Each [[detainee]] has the right to speak to a lawyer.

reply.context: Your friend calls from the airport: "Sorry, I'll be late. Border control won't let me through yet."
options: No worries, I'll detain the taxi outside until you get here.
Oh no, have they detained you? Is it something to do with your visa?
Please be advised that your detention has been noted in our records.
reply.explanationRu: Detain — официально задержать человека, как на границе. Такси не detain, его просят подождать, а третий ответ звучит как письмо из госучреждения.

definitionEn: the process of discovering or noticing something that is hidden or hard to see
situation: Doctors, scientists or security systems find something hidden, such as a disease, a crime or a leak.

examples.text: Early [[detection]] of the disease greatly improves the chances of survival.
Leak [[detection]] systems can save homeowners thousands in water damage.
Airport scanners have improved the [[detection]] of hidden weapons in luggage.

texts: The virus spread for weeks before [[detection]].
The thief was careful to avoid [[detection]].
Better cameras have made speed [[detection]] almost automatic.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Сделать открытие» — make a discovery. Detection — процесс обнаружения скрытого, с make не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Escape (или avoid) detection — остаться незамеченным. Finding — находка, opening — открытие магазина, а noticing после escape не употребляют.

nuance.text: Smoke [[detection]] is the job of a small sensor in the ceiling.
nuance.explanationRu: Detection — обнаружение: датчик замечает дым, анализ выявляет болезнь. Investigation — расследование, долгое выяснение обстоятельств.

reverse.text: Police have launched an [[investigation]] into the fire.
reverse.explanationRu: Расследование начинают: launch an investigation into something. Detection — сам факт обнаружения, его не «запускают».

fixIt.text: Thanks to the early [[revelation]] of the tumour, she needed only minor surgery.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Раннее выявление» болезни — early detection. Revelation — откровение или разоблачение, к медицине не подходит.

wordFormation.text: Dogs are trained in the [[detection]] of explosives and drugs.

rewrite.original: Nobody noticed what the thieves were doing for two years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Escape или avoid detection — остаться незамеченным.

definitionEn: the state of being kept in prison or another official place, often without trial
senseNote: Также — наказание в школе: остаться после уроков (get a detention). Здесь — содержание под стражей.
situation: Someone is held by the police or the state, for example in a cell, camp or special centre.

examples.text: The suspect will remain in [[detention]] until his case goes to court.
Lawyers were not allowed to visit him during his [[detention]].
Passengers without valid visas were taken to a [[detention]] room at the airport.

texts: The journalist was freed after ten days in [[detention]].
Rights groups criticised the [[detention]] of peaceful protesters.
Conditions in the [[detention]] centre were described as appalling.

badCollocation.noteRu: Задержка зарплаты — late payment of wages или delayed wages. Detention — содержание человека под стражей.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Held in detention (или custody) — содержаться под стражей. Арест — under arrest, capture — «поимка», а hostage употребляют без in: held hostage.

nuance.text: After two years in [[detention]], she was finally released.
nuance.explanationRu: Arrest — сам момент задержания (make an arrest, under arrest). Detention — период, когда человека держат под стражей: two years in detention.

reverse.text: Police made three [[arrests]] after the match.
reverse.explanationRu: Задержать кого-то — make an arrest. Detention — не действие полиции, а сам срок содержания под стражей.

fixIt.text: He spent six months in [[conclusion]] before the case against him was dropped.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Заключение под стражу» — detention (или custody). Conclusion — «вывод» или «окончание», это ложный друг переводчика.

wordFormation.text: Human rights lawyers challenged the [[detention]] of the students.

rewrite.original: The police held him for two days without charging him.
rewrite.frame: He was held in ____ for two days without charge.
rewrite.explanationRu: Held in detention — содержался под стражей.

definitionEn: to gradually become worse in quality, condition or strength
situation: Someone's health, a relationship or an old building slowly gets worse over time.

examples.text: Her condition [[deteriorated]] overnight, and she was moved to intensive care.
Relations between the two departments have [[deteriorated]] so badly that they barely speak.
Wooden window frames begin to [[deteriorate]] if they are not painted every few years.

texts: Food will [[deteriorate]] quickly if the fridge breaks down.
Doctors warned that his eyesight could [[deteriorate]] further.
We cannot let the situation [[deteriorate]] into open conflict.

badCollocation.noteRu: Deteriorate — «ухудшаться» самому, без дополнения. «Ухудшить ситуацию» — worsen или make the situation worse.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Здоровье ухудшается — health deteriorates. Spoil — о еде или испорченном празднике, damage требует дополнения, descend — «спускаться».

nuance.text: Relations between the neighbours [[deteriorated]] after the argument over the fence.
nuance.explanationRu: «Отношения испортились» — relations deteriorated (или went sour). Spoil — испортить что-то (праздник, сюрприз) или об испортившейся еде.

reverse.text: Don't let one bad review [[spoil]] your whole weekend.
reverse.explanationRu: Испортить кому-то выходные или праздник — spoil. Deteriorate — ухудшаться само по себе, дополнения у него нет.

fixIt.text: His health [[aggravated]] quickly during the long winter.
fixIt.explanationRu: Aggravate — «усугубить» что-то (aggravate an injury), ему нужно дополнение. «Здоровье ухудшилось» — his health deteriorated.

wordFormation.text: Doctors noticed a sharp [[deterioration]] in her breathing overnight.

reply.context: A friend asks about your grandfather: "How is he doing after the operation?"
options: Much better, thanks! He's deteriorating really fast now.
His physiological condition has undergone a deterioration of moderate severity.
He was doing well, but he's deteriorated a bit since the weekend, so we're worried.
reply.explanationRu: Deteriorate — ухудшаться, поэтому «мы волнуемся» звучит логично. Радоваться, что дедушка deteriorating, — противоречие, а второй ответ звучит как медицинская справка.
